title: Jotai
description: Model state as atoms in Jotai, derive computed values, and avoid re-render storms with the value/set hooks.

data.text: Jotai is an atomic state manager: each atom is an independent piece of state, and components subscribe only to the atoms they read. Derived atoms are computed from other atoms, so business logic lives outside components.

data.caption: src/atoms/cart.ts
Components subscribe to individual atoms

data.text: Prefer `useAtomValue` when you only read and `useSetAtom` when you only write. `useAtom` is convenient but subscribes the component to both, which is the usual cause of unnecessary renders.

data.caption: An async read atom plus a scoped Provider

data.text: Suspend-based async atoms integrate with React Suspense, so render a `<Suspense>` boundary and an error boundary around consumers. On the server, pass a fresh `Provider` store per request so state does not leak between users.

data.title: Install Jotai
data.code:
npm install jotai
# Optional devtools
npm install -D jotai-devtools

rows: One huge store with many unrelated fields

terms.definition: A unit of state; a primitive atom holds a value, a derived atom computes one.
A write-only atom (first argument null) that encapsulates a state transition.
Hook that subscribes to an atom's value for read-only components.
Scopes a set of atoms to a React subtree; required for per-request isolation in SSR.

items.question: Does Jotai work with React Server Components?
items.answer: Atom definitions are plain JavaScript and can be imported anywhere, but hooks such as useAtomValue are client-side only. Server Components can read the initial values you pass down as props.

items.question: Jotai vs Zustand?
items.answer: Jotai models many independent values; Zustand models one store with actions. Both are small, and both avoid context re-renders when used with selectors.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Describe atoms as independently subscribable state, derived atoms as memoised computed values, and the Provider as the server-safety boundary.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Atoms are the unit of state; components subscribe individually.
Derived atoms compute values from other atoms.
Use a Provider per request when server rendering.
data.takeaway: Jotai's atomic model is the cleanest answer to "how do I avoid context re-renders?"
